feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: NPR news, audio, and podcasts. Coverage of breaking stories, national and world news, politics, business, science, technology, and extended coverage of major national and world events.

entry.title: US and Denmark reach deal to build US military presence in Greenland
entry.summary: President Donald Trump says he has a deal with Denmark to bolster the U.S. military presence in Greenland. The announcement comes after months of threatening to take the island by force from the NATO ally.

entry.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
entry.summary: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

entry.title: Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House
entry.summary: The president chalked the ban up to what he called unfavorable coverage, and he threatened that bans on other media companies could be coming.

entry.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
entry.summary: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.

entry.title: Syrian regime planned American journalist's kidnapping for weeks
entry.summary: New reporting finds the abduction of journalist Austin Tice was planned by the Syrian government for weeks.

entry.title: What expensive sulfur means for your dinner table
entry.summary: Oil supplies are falling, sulfur prices are threatening food costs, and we measure Lego against Hollywood

entry.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
entry.summary: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?

entry.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
entry.summary: A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.

entry.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
entry.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

entry.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
entry.summary: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman
